FACT-1.gloss: Each lemon sold generates 1.5 dollars profit for Carlos
FACT-1.verify_reason: $1.5 per lemon is the sale price, not profit; the problem states a separate $3/year watering/feeding cost that must be subtracted from lemon revenue to get actual net earnings, which this fact ignores.

FACT-2.gloss: Carlos's lemon tree grows 7 lemons per year

FACT-3.gloss: Carlos needs 90 dollars worth of lemons to break even
FACT-3.verify_reason: the problem requires covering both the $90 planting cost and the ongoing $3/year maintenance cost; stating that he only needs "$90 worth of lemons" ignores the annual cost that reduces net earnings.

FACT-4.gloss: 8.57 rounded up to the nearest whole number is 9
FACT-4.verify_reason: this value is derived from an incomplete calculation that omits the $3/year maintenance cost, so it is not a valid entailment of the problem's actual break-even requirement.

OP-1.gloss: 7 lemons times 1.5 dollars per lemon equals 10.5 dollars per year

OP-2.gloss: 90 dollars divided by 10.5 dollars per year equals approximately 8.57 years

RULE-1.gloss: If x's tree grows n lemons per year, x earns m dollars per lemon, n times m equals p dollars per year, x needs b dollars to break even, and b divided by p equals y years, then x needs y years to break even
RULE-1.verify_reason: it computes break-even years using gross lemon revenue only (n×m), failing to subtract the stated $3/year watering/feeding cost before dividing into the $90 planting cost.

RULE-2.gloss: If x needs y years to break even and y rounds up to z, then x needs z years to break even (since fractional years must be rounded up to a whole year)

INF-1.gloss: Carlos needs approximately 8.57 years to break even, from FACT-1, FACT-2, FACT-3, OP-1, OP-2, and RULE-1 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-2.gloss: Carlos needs 9 years to break even, from INF-1, FACT-4, and RULE-2 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens
